ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Conflict and Culture in Korean History Description: This course considers how accounts of conflict in Korean history reflect the value systems and perceptions among Koreans from the late sixteenth century to the late twentieth century. By discussing the narrative and rhetorical styles of four major accounts dealing with issues such as wars, family tensions and person tribulations at a given historical time, students will understand how Koreans have dealt with conflict throughout history. This course will emphasize not only the conflict in the historical events protrayed by the accounts, but the inner conflict of the authors in their narratives. Readings will be in English. Instructor: Jungwon Kim
